text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: high memory pressure from KV-map growth on hosted-runtime pool 'eu-west-2a'. Multiple worker processes OOM'd; autoscaler recycled 4 nodes. Detected around 08:42 UTC. Investigating.
Alex: I'm on pager. Noted customer impact funneling into support. Can someone grab live metrics (kv-map size, batch sizes, in-flight sessions)?
Jen: pulling metrics now. Initial look: median session kv-map jumped from ~120k entries to ~2.1M over 7m for a small subset of sessions. Continuous-batching windows spiked concurrently.
Matt: looks like a specific prompt pattern causes prefix amplification + heavy prefetch. Could be a new template in prod.
Liz: support is seeing 5 active tickets from high-Tier customers complaining about timeouts and 502s. Ticket IDs: RDW-3312, RDW-3313, RDW-3314. Not yet widespread but definitely high-severity for those customers.
Sam: tagging runtime team. Recommended immediate mitigation options: 1) apply per-session kv cap (soft limit) 2) throttle prefetch for long sessions 3) rollback last batch scheduler tweak deployed ~2h ago.
Alex: do 1 + 2 as hotfix. We'll canary at 10% of nodes then expand. Jen, can you push a runtime param change?
Jen: will do. Preparing a patch to set kv_map.max_entries=200000 and prefetch.max_context_tokens=2048 for hosted-runtime pool. Applying to canary set.
Jen: command I'm running:```bash
redwoodctl runtime patch --pool eu-west-2a --set "kv_map.max_entries=200000" --set "prefetch.max_context_tokens=2048" --selector canary=true
```
Jen: canary patch applied to 3 nodes. Observing memory.
Matt: adding a temporary continuous-batching cutoff: batch.max_seq_len=4096 for those nodes to avoid oversized batches.
Alex: good. Also enable logging for the offending session ids: grep for "session_expansion" patterns.
Jen: logs show repeated user-generated content that contains embedded transcripts ~100k tokens long causing prefix duplication. Example snippet (sanitized):```text
[user prompt begins] long meeting transcript... repeated quoting... [user prompt ends]
```
Marta: flagged 2 customers that likely triggered this pattern — both use transcript ingestion features. I've reached out to their CSMs.
Liz: support updated RDW-3312/3/4 with workaround: advise customers to chunk uploads and temporarily disable transcript auto-expand.
Alex: can we throttle prefetch on gateway level to reject/limit sessions with prompt token count > 50k? That would be faster than changing client code.
Matt: yes, gateway rule available. I'll push rule to drop prefetch for requests where client-provided approx_tokens > 50000. Applying now to canary.
Matt: gateway rule in place on canary. Early telemetry: kv_map growth stabilized on patched nodes. Memory trending down.
Jen: canary stable for 4m. Rolling to the rest of the pool now (30 nodes). Rolling batch at 2 nodes at a time.
incident-bot: Update: incident severity escalated from P2 -> P1 due to customer-impacting 502s on paid customers. Paging product-sre and customer-success.
Alex: copying escalation notes to oncall channel. Sam, coordinate with infra to hold autoscaler from destroying recycled nodes so we can pull heap dumps if needed.
Sam: autoscaler hold in place for 20m. Collecting heap dumps from 2 affected nodes. Command:```bash
redwoodctl node exec --node-id node-4832 -- "gcore -o /tmp/heap.dump $(pidof runtime)"
```
Jen: heap dumps collected and uploaded to s3://redwood-incident-dumps/4491209876/. Sharing link in private.
Liz: support notes: 7 customers saw degraded responses for ~12-18 minutes; 2 had retries that resulted in errors. We're drafting a customer communication and opening credit requests.
Marta: prepping a brief for CSMs. Will include timeline, root-cause hypothesis, and mitigation steps.
Alex: root-cause hypothesis so far: transcript ingestion + changed batching heuristics created an amplification loop where kv_map prefetch duplicated prefixes across session continuations, driving per-session KV growth and OOM. The recent batch scheduler tweak increased max batch sequence length which amplified the effect.
Jen: opening PR to harden prefetch logic with a new de-duplication check: if prefix token overlap > 70% skip prefetch. Also adding a per-session eviction watermark. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8421
Matt: for short-term we reverted the batch-scheduler tweak in the cluster config (rolled back at 08:58 UTC).
Alex: what about monitoring? We need an alert that trips earlier when per-session kv_map grows > 500k.
Sam: adding alert now (alert id ALRT-9007). Will set severity to warn at 500k, page at 1.2M.
incident-bot: Note: postmortem owner assignment required.
Alex: Jen and Matt will co-own the postmortem. Sam to own SLO/alert tuning. Liz/Marta will handle customer comms. I'll prepare the incident timeline.
Jen: follow-up tasks I'm creating: 1) PR for prefetch de-dupe 2) unit tests for large prompt patterns 3) add quota enforcement in gateway.
Matt: follow-ups: 1) benchmark batch-scheduler change with synthetic transcripts 2) add batch-length safety caps 3) post-deploy perf smoke tests.
Liz: support action items: customer emails, credits, update tickets.
Marta: preparing internal note for execs + CSMs. Draft ETA for customer comms: 90m.
Alex: thanks all. Current status: hotfix rolled, canary stable, full pool rolled, autoscaler hold released. Monitoring open for 2h. If no regressions, we'll de-escalate.
Jen: final note — we should consider adding heuristics to the ingestion pipeline to detect transcript-style inputs and chunk them before they hit prefetch. Filing epic.
Matt: thumbs up. :thumbsup:
Liz: adding final customer impact summary to incident ticket.
Alex: closing notes: postmortem to be drafted in 48h and shared with incident channel. Good job team. :white_check_mark:
